sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by immunostaining (L1); surface-display imaging in neurons confirmed (L2). No direct assay of ADAM23 catalytic or ligand-binding function reported in either clip.
sites.rationale: ADAM23 has a single extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 60 (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 59). Because neither L1 nor L2 names a residue or a loop, topology_derived applies and the junction is uniquely insert_after_residue = 59 (residue S → S). Python confirmed residue 59 = S and residue 60 = S, and the junction sits 734 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any steric constraint. L2's pHluorin construct independently corroborates this extracellular N-terminal placement, since pHluorin must be on the extracellular face to report surface versus endosomal localisation. L1 (PMC3086669): full-length ADAM23 carrying an HA-tag was transfected into HEK293 cells and shown to be surface-displayed by immunostaining with patient anti-LGI1 antibodies. No residue or loop is named. L2 (PMC11156761) independently reports a CaMKII-ADAM23-pHluorin construct (Addgene #185539) used for surface-display imaging in neurons; pHluorin must be extracellular to function as a surface reporter. ADAM23 is a type I single-pass TM protein (SP 1-59, EC 60-793, TM 794-814, IC 815-832) with exactly one extracellular terminus, so the junction is uniquely determined.

sources.claim: HEK293 cells were transfected with plasmids containing ADAM22 or ADAM23 (both constructs containing an HA-tag), or co-transfected with LGI1 and ADAM22 or LGI1 and ADAM23.

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are available (L1, L2). Neither names a specific residue or loop; both are consistent with a single topology-derived N-terminal extracellular junction (insert_after_residue = 59). L2 uses a large pHluorin (~240 aa) rather than a short epitope tag, but it independently validates the extracellular N-terminal face for fusion. No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger. The intracellular C-terminus (815-832) is not a surface-tag site and is not listed in other_positions because neither clip reports a cytoplasmic insertion or a function-abrogating insertion.
